claims.statement: tests/conftest.py's isolate_index_db autouse fixture redirects DOCSWEEP_INDEX_DB to a tmp_path-scoped file for every test; its docstring records that on 2026-07-26, the mere existence of a developer's real ~/.docsweep/index.db (independent of its contents) caused 22 test failures by making scan_records() read the developer's real project index instead of the test's isolated workspace, and all 653 tests passed once the index was moved aside, a failure mode invisible in CI because CI has no such index file.

tests/conftest.py's isolate_session_log_env autouse fixture clears CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID, CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR, DOCSWEEP_AI_SESSION_LOG, and CODEX_HOME and monkeypatches session_logs._home() to a nonexistent tmp_path directory, because several session resolvers match on the current working directory recorded in a session's own metadata file under the real home directory, which clearing environment variables alone would not isolate; only _home is patched rather than HOME/USERPROFILE wholesale to avoid perturbing unrelated tooling such as git config resolution.

resolve_writable_md() rejects any path containing a literal '..' path segment at the input stage before calling realpath, as a defense-in-depth measure distinct from realpath's own '..' resolution, and only accepts paths that resolve under a configured scan root and end in .md; on failure it raises PathScopeError with a generic message rather than listing the checked roots, so a failed resolution cannot be used to enumerate configured scan roots.

.githooks/pre-push is enabled per-clone via git config core.hooksPath .githooks (never committed as automatically active), and its header comment cites a 2026-07-16 v0.3.0 release where pushing without running pytest locally first led to five consecutive CI failures once latent bugs surfaced remotely; the hook exits 0 (allowing the push) if python/python3 or pytest is unavailable, and blocks the push only on an actual pytest -q failure, with git push --no-verify remaining an explicit escape hatch.

pyproject.toml's ruff lint config selects only rule groups E/F/I/UP/B and explicitly ignores E501, E402, F841, B008, UP035, and I001 within those, each with an inline rationale (E501: CJK line-width impracticality; E402: intentional lazy imports for startup time; B008: FastAPI's Query()/Body() default-argument idiom; I001: deferred to a future bulk ruff --fix pass) rather than a blanket suppression.

pyproject.toml's mypy config stops short of strict mode and sets ignore_missing_imports = true specifically to tolerate optional dependencies (mcp, sentence_transformers) that ship without type stubs, reflecting a staged rather than complete type-checking adoption.

pytest.ini_options sets addopts = '-ra --strict-markers --strict-config', which fails a test run immediately on an undeclared pytest marker or malformed pytest configuration rather than silently accepting it.
